simple.meaning: מָתוֹק (mâthôwq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “sweet.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 12 times across Judges, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Solomon, and 2 more, beginning at Judges 14:14. Its contexts include family line, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָתוֹק (H4966).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מָתוֹק (mâthôwq) / H4966 is traced through Judges 14:14, Judges 14:18, Psalms 19:11, Proverbs 16:24 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4966. mathoq or mathuq מָתוֺק adjective sweet , and noun [masculine] sweetness (on form see Lag BN 30, 60 , compare Ba NB 13, 36 ); — absolute ׳מ Judg 14:14 9 t.; feminine מְתוּקָה Eccl 5:11 ; plural מְתוּקִים Psa 19:11 ; — 1 sweet , of honey Judg 14:14 (where ׳מ = substantive a sweet thing ), 14:18 (both Samson's riddle), Prov 24:13 ; so = sweetness , Ezek 3:3 ; more Generally, מ ׳כָּלמַֿר Prov 27:7 every bitter thing is sweet to one hungry; figurative Psa 19:11 (God's commandments, sweeter than honey), compare Prov 16:24 (simile of pleasant words) מ ׳וּפִרְיוֺ לְחִכִּי Song 2:3 (i.e his caresses); לְמ מַר ׳שָׂמִים ׳וּמ לְמָ֑ר Isa 5:20 making bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter (obscuring moral distinctions; || רָ֑ע וְלַטּוֺב טוֺב לָרַע הָאֹמְרִים ). 2 = pleasant , sleep of the toiler Eccl 5:11 ; light 1:17 (|| אֶתהַֿשֶּׁמֶשׁ לִרְאוֺת לַעֵינַיִם טוֺב ).

occurrences.englishText: The men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, “What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?”
Moreover your servant is warned by them.
My son, eat honey, for it is good,
A full soul loathes a honeycomb;
When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil;
Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil;
He said to me, “Son of man, cause your belly to eat, and fill your bowels with this scroll that I give you.”
